name: 2013 masi livery
description: White fuselage with 'FIJI' in tall dark inline capitals over the forward windows and 'AIRWAYS' beneath; the rear fuselage and tail cone wrapped in dark masi (tapa cloth) pattern. The fin rust-red with the white masi rosette, a band of masi pattern across its top and the dark corner at its forward root; white engines ringed by a narrow masi band; dark winglets.

logos.description: The Fiji Airways masi symbol, designed by Makereta Matemosi: a white rosette on the rust field, an outer ring of triangles and short bars round a ring of rust, a small many-pointed star with a diamond at its centre. Upright, the same on both sides.

Masi (Fijian tapa cloth) pattern: rows of white geometric motifs (triangles, arrow and cross shapes, bars) on dark brown-black, as on the tapa cloth the brand is drawn from. The fin's top band, from the rust field's upper edge to the tip (the areas paint its dark ground).

Masi (Fijian tapa cloth) pattern: rows of white geometric motifs (triangles, arrow and cross shapes, bars) on dark brown-black, as on the tapa cloth the brand is drawn from. The panel round the rear fuselage and tail cone, belly to crown, carrying on up the fillet into the fin's forward root; its forward edge has a column of short dark bars a little ahead of it, like a tapa border.
A narrow ring of masi pattern round the nacelle, small dark motifs on white between two thin dark rings (the areas paint the rings), about x 0.24 to 0.49 of the nacelle.
The small oneworld roundel (a navy disc with the white swirl) just aft of the forward door, above the window line; Fiji Airways is a full member from April 2025.
A small Fijian flag (light blue ensign with the Union Flag and the shield) ahead of the forward door, on the window line, after the aircraft's island name in small dark capitals.

titles.style: The 'FIJI' wordmark: tall geometric capitals in dark brown-black, widely spaced, each stroke split lengthwise by a thin white line (an inline, like masi cloth's ruled lines); over the windows (they show through) behind the forward door.
'AIRWAYS' in plain geometric capitals, medium weight, dark brown-black, under 'FIJI' from just behind its 'F'.

A359.note: Measured on DQ-FAN (A350-900, left, 2024-04-16), checked on DQ-FAI (right, 2026-01-02) and DQ-FAM (2026-07-26). The A350 differs from the 737 MAX in ways people notice: 'AIRWAYS' is followed by three dots (aft of the word on both sides: 'AIRWAYS...' on the left, '...AIRWAYS' on the right); the masi corner at the fin's forward root is much bigger (the rust field's forward edge is upright, meeting the leading edge 35% up); the top masi band starts 70% up; the aft panel starts 10 m from the tail cone's end.

notes: Measured on the 737 MAX 8 (the commonest type: 5 of 14 jets, July 2026) from DQ-FAD (left, near side-on, 2025-09-28) fitted to shapes/B38M.json, checked on DQ-FAB (2026-05-19). 'FIJI' runs x 0.163 to 0.269 across the window line (the windows show through), capitals about 1.6 m tall; 'AIRWAYS' x 0.172 to 0.257 below the windows. The masi pattern's motifs are artwork (logo entries FJI/masi); the areas carry its dark ground, so the panel, fin band and engine band read as dark, as they do from a distance. The column of short dark bars just ahead of the aft panel (x 0.76) isn't drawn. The A350 has its own paint in `types` (A359). The A330s (DQ-FJT/FJV/FJW, and the 737-800) weren't measured: on DQ-FJW (2026-07-12) 'AIRWAYS' has no dots (a small (R) after it) and the aft panel starts at the last door, so they take this scheme as placed. Each jet carries its island name ('ISLAND OF GAU', 'ISLAND OF KADAVU'…) in small dark capitals under the cockpit, and its registration and type small and dark aft. The right side is mirrored from the left on the evidence of DQ-FAH (2023) and DQ-FAI (2026); belly white. A330-200 DQ-FJU wears the oneworld scheme (not drawn here).
history: Introduced with the rebrand from Air Pacific to Fiji Airways (logo announced August 2012, flown from 2013), the masi symbol by artist Makereta Matemosi; still current. New to Open Liveries in 2026-11 (no earlier approximation).
